chore(repo): add the module, the layout, and the make check gate

make check is build, lint and test, and every later iteration closes on it,
so it has to exist before the work that will use it.

The gofmt target reads git ls-files --cached --others rather than the index
alone. Reading the index means a new package stays invisible until it is
added, and in a tree with nothing committed the target checks zero files and
reports success. It also fails outright when the file list comes back empty,
because the failure worth guarding against here is a check that passes while
checking nothing.

Each linter was made to fail on a planted violation before being trusted: a
misformatted file, a Printf verb that does not match its argument, and a
comparison to a boolean constant.

PATH takes GOPATH/bin from go env rather than a guessed install location, so
make finds tool binaries from a non-interactive shell with no profile
sourced. backlog runs required commands that way.
